auditor: independent AI auditor (did not write the paper); a fresh one for every round

audits.summary: Runs are real and bit-reproducible and all prose numbers match the tables, but the heuristic and nominal rows of Table I were run at dt=0.1 instead of the captioned 0.05 (heuristic DI violation rate is 0.110 at 0.05, not 0.216). The abstract's claim that CT-CBF never violates over alpha in [0.5,10] and dt in [0.01,0.2] and the H1 refutation rest on two one-factor slices; off-slice cells violate (0.27 at alpha=10, dt=0.1; 0.386 at dt=0.2). The DT-CBF is also not imposed on the exact ZOH successor as described; all of this is fixable by cheap re-runs and text changes.

findings.where: paper/sections/results.tex Table I caption and text; results/runs.jsonl main + sweep_dth commands; method/run.py --dt default
findings.issue: Heuristic and nominal runs never pass --dt and run at the script default 0.1 s, while Table I is captioned dt=0.05 s. At dt=0.05 the heuristic DI violation rate is 0.110+/-0.010 (not 0.216+/-0.049), min clearance 0.205 (not 0.131), worst penetration 0.184 (not 0.401); the baseline was handicapped by a doubled control period and the quoted 0.216 in Results/H4/RESULTS.md is wrong for the stated setting.
findings.fix: Pass --dt 0.05 explicitly for heur and nominal, re-run main and sweep_dth, regenerate tables and update the text; set the script default to the paper default.

findings.issue: Claim that CT-CBF never violated safety for alpha in [0.5,10] and dt in [0.01,0.2] is supported only on two one-factor slices (alpha sweep at dt=0.05, dt sweep at alpha=2). With the same code, CT-CBF on the double integrator violates off-slice: 0.27 at alpha=10/dt=0.1, 0.386 at alpha=10/dt=0.2, 0.02 at alpha=5/dt=0.2, 0.006 at alpha=0.5/dt=0.2. The H1 'refuted' verdict is an artifact of the one-at-a-time design.
findings.fix: Run the joint alpha x dt grid for CT and DT, report it, and restate the abstract, conclusion and H1 verdict (supported when alpha and dt are large jointly).

findings.where: paper/sections/method.tex (DT-CBF), ablations.tex, limitations.tex; method/run.py di_filter and uni_filter
findings.issue: Paper says the DT condition is imposed on the exact ZOH successor. For the double integrator psi1 uses the zero-input predicted position p+dt*v rather than the true successor p+dt*v+0.5*dt^2*a, so the enforced invariant does not imply h(x_{k+1})>=(1-gamma)h(x_k); the unicycle version is an Euler step of the look-ahead point. The paper lists the dropped quadratic term as a candidate cause of violations although dropping a nonnegative term only tightens the constraint. The headline DT-violates result may be an artifact of this undisclosed approximation.
findings.fix: Describe psi1 exactly as implemented and drop 'exact', or implement the condition on the true ZOH successor and re-run; remove the dropped quadratic term from the candidate causes and name the successor mismatch.

findings.issue: 'Larger gains reduced the time to goal on the double integrator only' is inaccurate: unicycle time falls from 12.84 to 11.86 s between alpha=0.5 and 2 before plateauing. 'Most influential factor was selection' ignores that alpha moves DT-CBF violations from 0 to 0.85, comparable to selection (0.82).
findings.fix: Say the unicycle gain effect saturates above alpha=2, and limit the selection claim to 'larger than the effect of dt'.

findings.issue: Pre-registered H3 covered time to goal and minimum clearance decreasing monotonically; the paper restates only time to goal.
findings.fix: State H3 as registered and report the clearance trend from the sweep.

findings.issue: DT-CBF violations are shallow grazes (median penetration about 7 mm, max 1.7 cm at defaults; mean clearance -0.004 m at alpha=10) versus up to 0.40 m for the heuristic; the binary violation rate alone overstates the DT problem. d_th=2 heuristic has success rate 0.996 on DI (timeouts inflate time to goal), not mentioned. 'Violations rise slowly with dt' has adjacent steps within one std.
findings.fix: Report penetration depth alongside violation rate in the sweeps, mention the 0.996 success rate, and limit the dt trend claim to the end-to-end difference.

findings.issue: All 300 rows record git_commit 18d24b6 (scaffold) which does not contain method/run.py, so the code was uncommitted when run; 300 runs share 221 log files because same-second filenames collide; logs contain only the header because the script prints nothing.
findings.fix: Commit code before running, make log names unique per config, and print the metrics to stdout so logs carry real output.

findings.issue: Unicycle CBF filters use the nearest obstacle, not the critical one; the paper only implies this.
findings.fix: State the unicycle selection rule explicitly.

findings.issue: Table I and Fig. 1 are shrunk to near-illegible size by resizebox; page 4 holds only two small tables; Fig. 2/3 error bars use population std while tables use sample std.
findings.fix: Shorten method names or use table*, enlarge Fig. 1, rebalance floats, and use ddof=1 in make_sweeps.py.

findings.issue: Directly relevant sampled-data CBF work (Breeden et al., named in literature/landscape.md) is not cited because the arXiv API was rate-limited.
findings.fix: Add and verify the sampled-data CBF references and cite them where sampled-data safety margins are discussed.

audits.summary: All 600 registry runs re-executed bit-identically, every quoted number matches the generated tables, citations are verified and used in context, and the PDF is clean at 5 pages. Three claims are not supported: the unicycle 'no violations in any cell' result comes from a metric with a ~0.15 m buffer (barrier-level violations reach 46-100% of episodes), DT-CBF penetrations are called 'mostly shallow' while the saturated cells in the registry show 0.11-0.68 m, and 'not caused by sampling alone' is contradicted by a direct probe. All are fixable with text changes and one added metric.

findings.where: method/run.py:100-102,170-171; paper/sections/abstract.tex, results.tex (grid paragraph, H2), conclusion.tex, setup.tex (Metrics)
findings.issue: Unicycle violation_rate is measured at the axle against the raw obstacle radius while the barrier constrains the look-ahead point against radii inflated by L=0.15 m, so the metric has a ~0.13-0.15 m buffer that the double-integrator metric (violation = h<0, 1e-5 m counts) lacks; this is not disclosed. Measured at barrier level, DT-CBF on the unicycle violates in 46% of episodes at the default, 97% at alpha=2,dt=0.2 and ~100% for alpha>=5 (max penetration 0.045 m), and CT-CBF in 86-100% at alpha>=5,dt=0.2 (max 0.095 m). 'On the unicycle neither CBF filter violated in any cell' and 'H2 untestable on the unicycle' are artifacts of the buffer.
findings.fix: Add a barrier-level violation metric for the unicycle (look-ahead point vs inflated radius) to run.py, re-run the unicycle grid (about 2 minutes), report both metrics, state the buffer explicitly in the Metrics paragraph, and rewrite the unicycle claims in the abstract, results, H2 verdict and conclusion (H2 is testable and refuted on the unicycle at barrier level).

findings.where: paper/sections/abstract.tex, conclusion.tex ('mostly with shallow penetrations'); results.tex ('small in depth where measured ... violation rate and depth at the saturated cells were not tabulated')
findings.issue: Depth in the saturated DT-CBF cells is in results/runs.jsonl and is not shallow: mean worst penetration 0.109 m (alpha=10,dt=0.1) and 0.679 m (alpha=5 and 10, dt=0.2; max 0.76 m, same as the unfiltered controller's 0.759 m), with mean min clearance -0.05/-0.18 m and time to goal 5.79 s at dt=0.2. These cells contain more violating episodes than all shallow cells combined, so 'mostly shallow' is false by episode count; the violation rate there (1.00) is in fact tabulated in Table II.
findings.fix: Report worst penetration and min clearance for the whole grid (extend Table II or add a table), state that DT-CBF fails with nominal-like penetrations where alpha*dt>=1, and remove 'mostly with shallow penetrations' or restrict it to alpha*dt<1.

findings.where: paper/sections/ablations.tex (Period paragraph); limitations.tex ('The DT-CBF violations remain unexplained')
findings.issue: The inference 'DT-CBF is non-zero at alpha=10, dt=0.01 (0.36), so its violations are not caused by sampling alone' is unsupported and contradicted by a direct probe: outside the saturated cells violations occur between samples (rate at sample instants <=0.03 with ~1e-14 m depth), and at dt=0.005 s (= plant step, no between-sample check) the rate is exactly 0 for alpha=2,5,10. Median penetration at alpha=10,dt=0.01 is 4e-5 m. The reported DT rates at small dt depend on the 0.005 s check resolution.
findings.fix: Replace the sentence with the measured explanation (inter-sample dips of the sample-instant-only condition, vanishing when dt equals the integration step), add the at-sample vs inter-sample breakdown or a dt=0.005 row, note the dependence on check resolution, and update the limitations sentence.

findings.issue: The registered test for H1 is the one-factor sweeps, on which CT-CBF is 0.00 everywhere (refuted by the registered criterion); the paper substitutes the full grid post hoc and labels H1 'supported with a qualification' without saying the registered test was the slices.
findings.fix: State that H1 is refuted on the registered one-factor test and holds only as a joint alpha-and-dt effect in the post-hoc grid; label it 'partly supported'.

findings.issue: 'CT-CBF was safe unless alpha and dt were both large' omits the alpha=0.5, dt=0.2 cell (rate 0.006, 3 of 500 episodes, penetrations up to 0.25 m). Runs are deterministic on fixed scenarios, so this is a real event, not seed noise, and it is deeper than most other CT cells.
findings.fix: Mention the small-alpha, large-dt exception and its depth in the abstract or conclusion, and do not describe it as noise.

findings.issue: DT-CBF at alpha=2, dt<=0.02 is reported as 0.00 but is 0.004 (2 of 500 episodes, ~1e-5 m).
findings.fix: Say 'below 0.005' or show three decimals for these cells.

findings.issue: 'DT is faster, not slower' (7.542 vs 7.800 s) has no rh compare output; only violation_rate was compared. The auditor's own test supports the claim (Welch p=0.007, paired p=1e-4).
findings.fix: Generate compare_main_time_to_goal.csv and cite the p-value.

findings.issue: Label sec:setup is defined twice (LaTeX warning), and Tables I and V are scaled very small in the PDF.
findings.fix: Remove the duplicate label and enlarge or split the two tables.

audits.summary: All 630 runs are real, logged and bit-reproducible, every table matches the registry, citations are in context and the paper reports its negative result honestly. Two statements in the sample-instant analysis are not supported: the saturated-cell at-sample violations (0.760/0.830) called a genuine unexplained failure are floating-point round-off of about 1e-14 m, and the claimed bounds for alpha*dt<1 (any-time rate up to 0.358, penetration below 0.0005 m) contradict Table II (0.618, up to 0.016 m). findings.where: paper/sections/ablations.tex (Between samples or at samples?), limitations.tex, Table IV, results/RESULTS.md
findings.issue: The DT-CBF sample-instant violation rates in saturated cells (0.760 at alpha=5,dt=0.2; 0.830 at alpha=10,dt=0.1) are presented as evidence that the filter genuinely fails at samples for an unexplained reason. Re-simulation shows the worst at-sample penetration is about 1e-14 m and the rate is 0.000 with a 1e-9 tolerance in every double-integrator DT cell probed, including the 0.028 cell; it is round-off from projecting exactly onto the boundary plus a strict <0 test. The deep penetrations there are inter-sample.
findings.fix: Add a small tolerance (e.g. 1e-9) to sample_violation_rate in method/run.py or report at-sample penetration depth, re-run the grid, regenerate Table IV, and rewrite the ablation and limitation sentences to say the saturated-cell failures are also inter-sample (gamma=1 only requires the successor on the boundary).

# Response to the final audit round

All 660 runs were re-executed after the metric change (code commit 745cf32, recorded in every run); the previous 630 runs are archived in `results/archive_round3/`. Earlier responses are in the git history of this file.

## Major

1. **Saturated-cell at-sample violations were round-off - fixed in the metric, re-run, text rewritten.** Confirmed by re-simulation (worst at-sample penetration about 1e-14 m in every double-integrator DT-CBF cell that the old table showed as non-zero). `method/run.py` now counts a violation only if clearance < -1e-9 m, for all three violation rates and all systems, and also records `sample_penetration`. With the tolerance the DT-CBF at-sample rate on the double integrator is 0.000 in every cell of Table IV except alpha=10, dt=0.2 (0.002: one real episode in 500, at-sample depth 0.014 m, not investigated and stated as such). Any-time rates are unchanged. Ablations, Limitations, abstract, conclusion and RESULTS.md now say that the saturated-cell failures are inter-sample too (gamma=1 only requires the successor on the boundary; the "why deep" mechanism carries "may"). Limitations records the earlier wrong reading. The dt=0.005 s probe was extended to the unicycle (30 extra runs), which shows the opposite regime there: DT-CBF violations are at the samples and remain at dt = plant step.
2. **Wrong bounds for alpha*dt<1 - fixed.** Text now gives the Table II maxima: any-time rate up to 0.618 (alpha=10, dt=0.05), mean worst penetration up to 0.016 m (alpha=2, dt=0.2), and 0.000 m at three decimals only for dt<=0.02. Same numbers in Results, abstract and conclusion.

## Minor

3. **Period, adjacent steps - fixed.** Now: steps up to dt=0.1 are within the seed spread, the last step (0.018 to 0.070) exceeds it.
4. **Hypothesis tally - fixed.** Introduction, Results, BRIEF.md and RESULTS.md agree: H2 refuted; H1, H3, H4 partly supported, with H1 and H4 failing their stated tests as written and H3 holding on the double integrator only. Each verdict in Results now names the stated test first.
5. **100 unicycle cells - fixed** (50).
6. **CT-CBF at-sample sentence - fixed.** Scoped to the gains of Table IV; the alpha=0.5, dt=0.2 cell is mentioned as also having at-sample violations.
7. **Run time - fixed.** "typically under one second (a few seconds at most)"; registry durations in this round: median 0.4 s, one run 4.8 s.
8. **Pre-registration claims - fixed.** "as stated in the proposal"; "fixed before running" removed; Limitations states that hypotheses were first committed together with the first results and that the round-1 script default was dt=0.1 s.
9. **Design-order confound - fixed.** Named in the abstract, the H2 verdict, Method, Limitations and conclusion ("first-order discrete-time condition" vs "second-order continuous-time filter"). A high-order DT-CBF was not implemented (out of budget for this round); stated.
10. **"One linear constraint" - fixed.** Now one scalar constraint with a closed-form projection (half-space / ball exterior).
11. **0.679 m - fixed.** Called "mean worst penetration" everywhere (table captions define it as the mean over seeds of each seed's deepest violation); the single-seed maximum 0.760 m is in RESULTS.md.
12. **Singletary et al. - fixed.** "analytically and with supporting experiments".
13. **Table I legibility - fixed.** Systems are registered under short names (Nominal, Braking, CT-CBF, DT-CBF; defined in Setup and the caption); the table now scales to about 85% instead of being unreadable. Tables III and V were transposed to single-column tables at footnotesize.

## Found in the self-audit

- Table V (braking threshold) was captioned "barrier level" but used the axle metrics; it now uses the barrier-level metrics (values on these rows are identical).
- "DT-CBF was not safer on either plant" contradicted the one cell where it is lower; abstract and conclusion now say "lower in one grid cell only".
- "at most 0.035 m" for unicycle DT-CBF depth ignored the alpha=1, dt=0.2 cell; now "at most 0.043 m over the whole grid".
- "nearly zero for alpha<=1" is exactly zero; "grows" replaced by "does not decrease".
- Removed an unverifiable anecdote about an early version and two mechanism sentences without a run; the unicycle Euler-successor explanation carries "may" and "consistent with".
- PROTOCOL.md said 600 runs; it now lists the groups and 660 runs.
- Setup now states that time to goal is resolved to dt and how the plants are integrated.
